+# Daily Grind
+
+The homepage loads `analytics.js` as a deferred script. It records one `page_view`
+and delegated `click` events, including nested link/button clicks, without changing
+navigation behavior. Events contain an ISO timestamp, page pathname, and (for
+clicks) target tag, optional element ID, and link destination pathname. Query
+strings, hashes, text content, and form values are excluded.
+
+Configure your deployment to accept JSON `POST` requests at `/api/analytics`
+(change `ENDPOINT` in `analytics.js` to use a different collector). This static
+repository does not include a server-side collector. The request body is:
+
+```json
+{"events":[{"type":"page_view","timestamp":"2026-11-06T00:00:00.000Z","path":"/"}]}
+```
+
+Each event replaces the pending request with the full batch and restarts a
+one-second inactivity window. Native `fetchLater()` sends on timeout or departure;
+other browsers use a timer and flush on page hide with a low-priority keepalive
+fetch. Full batches (100 events or 48 KiB) are dispatched before starting another.
+Quota errors fall back to the compatibility transport. Failed requests are not
+retried, so analytics remains best-effort and cannot create a retry storm.
+
+Run the isolated, browser-free checks with `node --test analytics.test.cjs`.

+The homepage loads `analytics.js` with `defer`. It records a `page_view` on
+load (and back/forward cache restoration) and delegated `click` events.
+Links use stable `data-analytics` labels. Events contain an ISO timestamp,
+the page pathname, and, for clicks, the target tag, optional label, and
+same-origin destination pathname. URL queries, fragments, text, and form values
+are excluded.
+
+Configure the hosting service to accept `POST /api/analytics` with JSON:
+
+```json
+{"events":[{"type":"page_view","timestamp":"2026-11-06T00:00:00.000Z","page":"/"}]}
+```
+
+This static repository does not include a collector. Change `ENDPOINT` in
+`analytics.js` if the hosting service provides a different collection route.
+
+Events debounce for 750 ms, then send during browser idle time (with a 1-second
+idle deadline or a timer fallback). A 5-second maximum wait prevents sustained
+interaction from starving delivery. Requests contain up to 50 events; the queue
+retains at most the latest 200 events. Remaining batches are deferred again.
+Hiding or leaving the page flushes pending batches with `sendBeacon`, falling
+back to a keepalive fetch. Normal fetches omit credentials. Delivery is best
+effort without retries, so collector failures never interrupt user interaction.
+
+Run automated checks with `node --test analytics.test.cjs`. They use simulated
+DOM events and timers; no browser or development server is required.

+# The Daily Grind
+
+Static homepage with a browser-only encrypted delivery-notes demonstration.
+
+## Build
+
+Install the pinned dependencies with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then run
+`pnpm build`. The build bundles the cryptographic implementation into
+`assets/delivery-notes.js`; the checked-in bundle lets the existing static hosting
+setup serve the feature without runtime package downloads. Serve the site over
+HTTPS (or localhost) for WebCrypto. No experimental browser flags are required.
+
+## Delivery notes
+
+- Hybrid (default): noble's X-Wing construction, ML-KEM-768 + X25519.
+- Post-quantum: ML-KEM-768.
+- Classical: native WebCrypto ephemeral-static ECDH P-256, explicitly labeled as
+  lacking post-quantum protection. Modes never silently downgrade.
+- All modes derive a non-extractable AES-256-GCM key through HKDF-SHA-256 with a
+  fresh 32-byte salt and application-specific context. Each encryption uses a
+  fresh encapsulation/agreement, a 12-byte random nonce, and a 128-bit GCM tag.
+- The authenticated metadata includes the protocol version, suite, recipient
+  fingerprint, note ID, timestamp, capsule, and salt. Tampered metadata or
+  ciphertext cannot be revealed successfully.
+- Before showing success, the demo decapsulates and decrypts the envelope with
+  the separate recipient private key, confirming that the original note matches.
+- Notes, envelopes, and recipient keys stay in page memory. No localStorage,
+  IndexedDB, cookies, analytics, or network submissions store customer text.
+  Keys are discarded when notes are replaced or deleted, or on page exit.
+  JavaScript memory erasure is best effort; strings and CryptoKeys are managed
+  by the browser. Downloaded envelopes contain no private key and cannot be
+  decrypted after the demo session ends.
+- Rendering uses textContent. Controls fail closed if JavaScript or WebCrypto
+  is unavailable, and the Content Security Policy blocks form and fetch uploads.
+
+## Production integration boundary
+
+This repository has no order API, authenticated account system, or delivery-team
+key service. This feature is deliberately labeled a local demo and does not
+claim that a courier received a note.
+
+For real delivery, generate and retain the recipient's private keys in the
+recipient's trusted environment, rather than the customer's browser. Publish
+and authenticate a versioned recipient public-key record through a trusted
+channel. Pass only that public key and its verified fingerprint to `sealNote`.
+Send the resulting envelope through an authenticated order endpoint that binds
+it to the authorized order and recipient, validates lengths and suites, and
+handles retention, key rotation, authorization, and replay prevention. Extend
+authenticated metadata to include that order identity. Remove the demo's local
+recipient and reveal flow, and permit only the required API in the CSP.
+
+Encryption does not protect against compromised page scripts, malicious browser
+extensions, an already compromised endpoint, or an unauthenticated replacement
+recipient key. The demo is not a security-audited production protocol.
+
+Stock photography is served by Unsplash; Google Fonts supplies typography.
+Neither receives note text, and the page sends no referrer header.

@@ -0,0 +1,98 @@
+import { ml_kem768_x25519 } from '@noble/post-quantum/hybrid.js';
+import { ml_kem768 } from '@noble/post-quantum/ml-kem.js';
+
+export const suites = {
+  hybrid: 'X-Wing+HKDF-SHA256+AES-256-GCM',
+  'post-quantum': 'ML-KEM-768+HKDF-SHA256+AES-256-GCM',
+  classical: 'ECDH-P256+HKDF-SHA256+AES-256-GCM',
+};
+const encoder = new TextEncoder();
+const kemFor = (mode) => mode === 'hybrid' ? ml_kem768_x25519 : ml_kem768;
+const random = (size) => crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(size));
+export const toBase64 = (bytes) => btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes));
+const fromBase64 = (text) => Uint8Array.from(atob(text), (c) => c.charCodeAt(0));
+
+export async function createRecipient(mode) {
+  if (!Object.hasOwn(suites, mode)) throw new Error('Unsupported protection mode');
+  const pair = mode === 'classical'
+    ? await crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: 'ECDH', namedCurve: 'P-256' }, false, ['deriveBits'])
+    : kemFor(mode).keygen();
+  const publicKey = mode === 'classical'
+    ? new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.exportKey('raw', pair.publicKey))
+    : pair.publicKey;
+  const digest = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', publicKey));
+  return { mode, publicKey, privateKey: pair.privateKey ?? pair.secretKey, id: toBase64(digest) };
+}
+
+function metadata(envelope) {
+  return encoder.encode(JSON.stringify({
+    version: envelope.version, suite: envelope.suite, recipientId: envelope.recipientId,
+    noteId: envelope.noteId, createdAt: envelope.createdAt, capsule: envelope.capsule,
+    salt: envelope.salt,
+  }));
+}
+
+async function deriveKey(secret, salt, usage) {
+  try {
+    const material = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', secret, 'HKDF', false, ['deriveKey']);
+    return await crypto.subtle.deriveKey({
+      name: 'HKDF', hash: 'SHA-256', salt,
+      info: encoder.encode('daily-grind/delivery-notes/envelope-v1'),
+    }, material, { name: 'AES-GCM', length: 256 }, false, [usage]);
+  } finally { secret.fill(0); }
+}
+
+// Sender receives ONLY the public key and its authenticated identifier.
+export async function sealNote({ mode, publicKey, id }, note) {
+  if (!Object.hasOwn(suites, mode)) throw new Error('Unsupported protection mode');
+  if (typeof note !== 'string' || !note.trim() || note.length > 500) throw new Error('Enter a note of 1–500 characters.');
+  let capsule, secret;
+  if (mode === 'classical') {
+    const peer = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', publicKey, { name: 'ECDH', namedCurve: 'P-256' }, false, []);
+    const ephemeral = await crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: 'ECDH', namedCurve: 'P-256' }, false, ['deriveBits']);
+    capsule = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.exportKey('raw', ephemeral.publicKey));
+    secret = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.deriveBits({ name: 'ECDH', public: peer }, ephemeral.privateKey, 256));
+  } else {
+    const result = kemFor(mode).encapsulate(publicKey);
+    capsule = result.cipherText;
+    secret = result.sharedSecret;
+  }
+  const salt = random(32), iv = random(12);
+  const envelope = {
+    version: 1, suite: suites[mode], recipientId: id,
+    noteId: toBase64(random(16)), createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
+    capsule: toBase64(capsule), salt: toBase64(salt), iv: toBase64(iv),
+  };
+  const key = await deriveKey(secret, salt, 'encrypt');
+  const plaintext = encoder.encode(note);
+  try {
+    const ciphertext = await crypto.subtle.encrypt({ name: 'AES-GCM', iv, additionalData: metadata(envelope), tagLength: 128 }, key, plaintext);
+    return { ...envelope, ciphertext: toBase64(new Uint8Array(ciphertext)) };
+  } finally { plaintext.fill(0); }
+}
+
+export async function openNote(recipient, envelope) {
+  if (envelope.version !== 1 || envelope.suite !== suites[recipient.mode] || envelope.recipientId !== recipient.id) {
+    throw new Error('The encryption envelope does not match its recipient.');
+  }
+  const iv = fromBase64(envelope.iv), salt = fromBase64(envelope.salt);
+  if (iv.length !== 12 || salt.length !== 32) throw new Error('Invalid encryption parameters.');
+  const capsule = fromBase64(envelope.capsule);
+  let secret;
+  if (recipient.mode === 'classical') {
+    const peer = await crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', capsule, { name: 'ECDH', namedCurve: 'P-256' }, false, []);
+    secret = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.deriveBits({ name: 'ECDH', public: peer }, recipient.privateKey, 256));
+  } else {
+    secret = kemFor(recipient.mode).decapsulate(capsule, recipient.privateKey);
+  }
+  const key = await deriveKey(secret, salt, 'decrypt');
+  const plaintext = new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.decrypt({
+    name: 'AES-GCM', iv, additionalData: metadata(envelope), tagLength: 128,
+  }, key, fromBase64(envelope.ciphertext)));
+  try { return new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: true }).decode(plaintext); }
+  finally { plaintext.fill(0); }
+}
+
+export function destroyRecipient(recipient) {
+  if (recipient?.privateKey instanceof Uint8Array) recipient.privateKey.fill(0);
+}

+import { createRecipient, sealNote, openNote, destroyRecipient } from './crypto.js';
+
+const $ = (id) => document.getElementById(id);
+const form = $('notes-form'), fields = $('notes-fields'), note = $('delivery-note');
+const protection = $('protection'), status = $('note-status'), button = $('encrypt-button');
+const saved = $('saved-note'), reveal = $('reveal-note'), decrypted = $('decrypted-note');
+const descriptions = {
+  hybrid: 'Combines classical and post-quantum protection for your shared secret.',
+  'post-quantum': 'Uses ML-KEM-768 for a post-quantum shared secret.',
+  classical: 'Uses P-256 key agreement. This mode does not provide post-quantum protection.',
+};
+let current = null, busy = false;
+const announce = (message, error = false) => {
+  status.textContent = message;
+  status.classList.toggle('error', error);
+};
+const resetReveal = () => {
+  decrypted.textContent = '';
+  decrypted.hidden = true;
+  reveal.textContent = 'Verify & reveal note';
+  reveal.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
+};
+const updateCount = () => { $('note-count').textContent = `${note.value.length} / 500`; };
+
+// Fail closed: controls remain disabled unless the local bundle and WebCrypto load.
+form.addEventListener('submit', async (event) => {
+  event.preventDefault();
+  if (busy) return;
+  if (!note.value.trim()) {
+    note.setCustomValidity('Please enter a delivery note.');
+    note.reportValidity();
+    return;
+  }
+  busy = true;
+  fields.disabled = true;
+  button.setAttribute('aria-busy', 'true');
+  announce('Establishing a fresh shared secret and encrypting your note…');
+  let recipient;
+  try {
+    recipient = await createRecipient(protection.value);
+    const { mode, publicKey, id } = recipient;
+    const envelope = await sealNote({ mode, publicKey, id }, note.value);
+    // Confirm the full recipient flow before replacing the previous encrypted note.
+    if (await openNote(recipient, envelope) !== note.value) throw new Error('Verification failed');
+    destroyRecipient(current?.recipient);
+    current = { recipient, envelope };
+    recipient = null;
+    resetReveal();
+    $('envelope-output').textContent = JSON.stringify(envelope, null, 2);
+    const names = { hybrid: 'Hybrid', 'post-quantum': 'Post-quantum', classical: 'Classical' };
+    $('saved-info').textContent = `${names[mode]} protection · ${new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, { hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit' }).format(new Date(envelope.createdAt))} · This page session only`;
+    saved.hidden = false;
+    note.value = '';
+    updateCount();
+    announce('Your note is encrypted and verified. Nothing has been sent to a delivery team.');
+  } catch {
+    announce('We couldn’t encrypt your note. Your draft is still here; please try again. Nothing was sent.', true);
+  } finally {
+    destroyRecipient(recipient);
+    busy = false;
+    fields.disabled = false;
+    button.removeAttribute('aria-busy');
+  }
+});
+note.addEventListener('input', () => { note.setCustomValidity(''); updateCount(); });
+protection.addEventListener('change', () => { $('protection-description').textContent = descriptions[protection.value]; });
+reveal.addEventListener('click', async () => {
+  if (!current) return;
+  if (!decrypted.hidden) { resetReveal(); return; }
+  const snapshot = current;
+  reveal.disabled = true;
+  try {
+    const plaintext = await openNote(snapshot.recipient, snapshot.envelope);
+    if (current !== snapshot) return;
+    decrypted.textContent = plaintext;
+    decrypted.hidden = false;
+    reveal.textContent = 'Hide note';
+    reveal.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
+    announce('Note decrypted. Its authentication tag and metadata were verified.');
+  } catch { announce('This note could not be authenticated. It has not been revealed.', true); }
+  finally { reveal.disabled = false; }
+});
+$('clear-note').addEventListener('click', () => {
+  destroyRecipient(current?.recipient);
+  current = null;
+  resetReveal();
+  $('envelope-output').textContent = '';
+  $('saved-info').textContent = '';
+  saved.hidden = true;
+  announce('Encrypted note and demo recipient key deleted from this page.');
+  note.focus();
+});
+$('download-note').addEventListener('click', () => {
+  if (!current) return;
+  const blob = new Blob([JSON.stringify(current.envelope, null, 2)], { type: 'application/json' });
+  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob), link = document.createElement('a');
+  link.href = url;
+  link.download = 'daily-grind-encrypted-note.json';
+  link.click();
+  setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 1000);
+  announce('Encrypted copy downloaded. Demo keys are not included; the copy cannot be decrypted after this page closes.');
+});
+// Do not let a back/forward-cache restore retain notes, revealed text, or keys.
+window.addEventListener('pagehide', () => {
+  destroyRecipient(current?.recipient);
+  current = null;
+  note.value = '';
+  updateCount();
+  resetReveal();
+  $('envelope-output').textContent = '';
+  $('saved-info').textContent = '';
+  saved.hidden = true;
+});
+window.addEventListener('pageshow', (event) => {
+  if (event.persisted) announce('Previous session cleared. Ready to encrypt a new note.');
+});
+if (globalThis.isSecureContext && globalThis.crypto?.subtle) {
+  fields.disabled = false;
+  announce('Ready when you are. Your note stays in this page session.');
+} else {
+  announce('Encryption requires a secure HTTPS connection or localhost. The form is disabled.', true);
+}

-# The DevTools Times
+# smallpt in your browser
 
-This project is a sample news application built with Astro, designed to serve as a testing ground for new features in Chrome DevTools.
+Kevin Beason’s C++ path tracer, compiled to WebAssembly with Emscripten. The Astro home page is prerendered to `dist/client/index.html`. The existing deployment base is `/devtools-times/`.
 
+The renderer runs entirely on the client in a module worker. Each pass adds four samples per pixel. Randomize changes the mirror and glass sphere reflectance, preserving their original materials and the Cornell box. Settings restart rendering; reset restores the original scene. PNG export saves the current render.
+
+## Build
+
+```sh
+pnpm install
+pnpm build
+```
+
+Compiled WebAssembly and its JavaScript loader are checked in under `public/wasm`, so the app build does not require a C++ toolchain. To rebuild the renderer with Emscripten installed:
 
 ```sh
-pnpm install && pnpm run start
+pnpm build:wasm
+node scripts/test-wasm.mjs
 ```
 
-The application will now be running on `http://localhost:11224`.
+`renderer/smallpt-original.cpp` is the unmodified upstream source. `renderer/smallpt.cpp` adds the progressive RGBA adapter, seeded color control, and a depth cap to bound stack usage. The initial preview is rendered from this same C++ source at 128 samples per pixel, and live output replaces it as soon as the first pass completes.
+
+To regenerate the initial preview (requires `g++` and Python 3):
 
-## Tech Stack
+```sh
+g++ renderer/smallpt.cpp -O3 -DSMALLPT_PREVIEW -o /tmp/smallpt-preview
+/tmp/smallpt-preview
+python3 scripts/convert-preview.py
+```

+import createSmallpt from './smallpt.js';
+
+self.onmessage = async ({ data }) => {
+  try {
+    const { width, height, samples, seed, colored } = data;
+    const engine = await createSmallpt();
+    engine._init(width, height, seed, colored ? 1 : 0);
+    const colors = [0, 1].map(sphere => [0, 1, 2].map(channel => engine._get_color(sphere, channel)));
+    self.postMessage({ type: 'ready', colors });
+    const passes = samples / 4;
+    for (let pass = 0; pass < passes; pass++) {
+      for (let row = 0; row < height; row += 8) {
+        engine._render_rows(row, Math.min(8, height - row));
+        self.postMessage({ type: 'progress', progress: (pass + Math.min(row + 8, height) / height) / passes });
+      }
+      const pixels = engine.HEAPU8.slice(engine._get_pixels(), engine._get_pixels() + width * height * 4);
+      self.postMessage({ type: 'frame', pixels, samples: (pass + 1) * 4, done: pass === passes - 1 }, [pixels.buffer]);
+    }
+  } catch (error) {
+    self.postMessage({ type: 'error', message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) });
+  }
+};

+  Vec operator+(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x+b.x,y+b.y,z+b.z); }
+  Vec operator-(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x-b.x,y-b.y,z-b.z); }
+  Vec operator*(double b) const { return Vec(x*b,y*b,z*b); }
+  Vec mult(const Vec &b) const { return Vec(x*b.x,y*b.y,z*b.z); }
+  Vec& norm(){ return *this = *this * (1/sqrt(x*x+y*y+z*z)); }
+  double dot(const Vec &b) const { return x*b.x+y*b.y+z*b.z; } // cross:
+  Vec operator%(Vec&b){return Vec(y*b.z-z*b.y,z*b.x-x*b.z,x*b.y-y*b.x);}
+};
+struct Ray { Vec o, d; Ray(Vec o_, Vec d_) : o(o_), d(d_) {} };

+  double rad;       // radius
+  Vec p, e, c;      // position, emission, color
+  Refl_t refl;      // reflection type (DIFFuse, SPECular, REFRactive)
+  Sphere(double rad_, Vec p_, Vec e_, Vec c_, Refl_t refl_):
+    rad(rad_), p(p_), e(e_), c(c_), refl(refl_) {}
+  double intersect(const Ray &r) const { // returns distance, 0 if nohit
+    Vec op = p-r.o; // Solve t^2*d.d + 2*t*(o-p).d + (o-p).(o-p)-R^2 = 0
+    double t, eps=1e-4, b=op.dot(r.d), det=b*b-op.dot(op)+rad*rad;
+    if (det<0) return 0; else det=sqrt(det);
+    return (t=b-det)>eps ? t : ((t=b+det)>eps ? t : 0);
+  }
+};

+  Sphere(1e5, Vec( 1e5+1,40.8,81.6), Vec(),Vec(.75,.25,.25),DIFF),//Left
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(-1e5+99,40.8,81.6),Vec(),Vec(.25,.25,.75),DIFF),//Rght

+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,40.8,-1e5+170), Vec(),Vec(),           DIFF),//Frnt
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50, 1e5, 81.6),    Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Botm
+  Sphere(1e5, Vec(50,-1e5+81.6,81.6),Vec(),Vec(.75,.75,.75),DIFF),//Top

+  Sphere(16.5,Vec(73,16.5,78),       Vec(),Vec(1,1,1)*.999, REFR),//Glas

+          } // Camera rays are pushed ^^^^^ forward to start in interior
+          c[i] = c[i] + Vec(clamp(r.x),clamp(r.y),clamp(r.z))*.25;
+        }
+  }

+  fprintf(f, "P3\n%d %d\n%d\n", w, h, 255);

+}

+assert len(pixels) == width * height * 3

+def chunk(kind, data):
+    return (struct.pack('>I', len(data)) + kind + data
+            + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(kind + data) & 0xffffffff))
+
+Path('public/render-preview.png').write_bytes(

+    + chunk(b'IDAT', zlib.compress(scanlines, 9))

+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
+import createSmallpt from '../public/wasm/smallpt.js';
+const engine = await createSmallpt({ wasmBinary: await readFile(new URL('../public/wasm/smallpt.wasm', import.meta.url)) });
+function frame(seed, colored) {
+  engine._init(32, 24, seed, colored);
+  for (let row = 0; row < 24; row += 8) engine._render_rows(row, 8);
+  return engine.HEAPU8.slice(engine._get_pixels(), engine._get_pixels() + 32 * 24 * 4);
+}
+const original = frame(420, 0);
+assert(original.some((v, i) => i % 4 !== 3 && v > 0), 'Renderer must produce visible pixels');
+assert(original.every((v, i) => i % 4 !== 3 || v === 255), 'All pixels must be opaque');
+const randomized = frame(917, 1);
+assert.notDeepEqual(original, randomized, 'Random colors must change the rendered output');
+assert(engine._get_color(0, 0) < .999, 'Mirror color must be randomized');
+assert(engine._get_color(1, 0) < .999, 'Glass color must be randomized');
+assert.deepEqual(frame(420, 0), original, 'Reset must reproduce the original scene');
+engine._render_rows(0, 24);
+assert.notDeepEqual(engine.HEAPU8.slice(engine._get_pixels(), engine._get_pixels() + 32 * 24 * 4), original, 'Additional passes must refine the render');
+console.log('WASM checks passed: visible RGBA output, randomized colors, deterministic reset, progressive rendering.');

+const canvas = document.querySelector<HTMLCanvasElement>('#render-canvas')!;
+const context = canvas.getContext('2d')!;
+const samples = document.querySelector<HTMLSelectElement>('#samples')!;
+const resolution = document.querySelector<HTMLSelectElement>('#resolution')!;
+const state = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#render-state')!;
+const sampleStatus = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#sample-status')!;
+const elapsed = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#elapsed')!;
+const progress = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#render-progress')!;
+const dot = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#status-dot')!;
+const base = import.meta.env.BASE_URL;
+let worker: Worker | undefined;
+let timer: ReturnType<typeof setInterval>;
+let colored = false;
+let seed = 420;
+let hasFrame = false;
+let started = 0;
+
+function render() {
+  worker?.terminate();
+  clearInterval(timer);
+  const width = Number(resolution.value);
+  const height = width * 3 / 4;
+  const total = Number(samples.value);
+  hasFrame = false;
+  state.textContent = 'Loading WebAssembly';
+  dot.style.background = '#9ba86f';
+  sampleStatus.textContent = `0 / ${total} samples`;
+  document.querySelector('#resolution-status')!.textContent = `${width} × ${height}`;
+  progress.style.width = '0%';
+  started = performance.now();
+  elapsed.textContent = '0.0s';
+  timer = setInterval(() => { elapsed.textContent = `${((performance.now() - started) / 1000).toFixed(1)}s`; }, 100);
+  const fail = (message: string) => {
+    clearInterval(timer);
+    state.textContent = 'Renderer unavailable';
+    state.title = message;
+    dot.style.background = '#ba7860';
+    sampleStatus.textContent = 'Click randomize to retry';
+    worker?.terminate();
+  };
+  try {
+    worker = new Worker(`${base}wasm/render-worker.js`, { type: 'module' });
+    worker.onerror = (event) => fail(event.message);
+    worker.onmessage = ({ data }) => {
+      if (data.type === 'ready') {
+        state.textContent = 'Tracing light';
+        data.colors.forEach((color: number[], i: number) => {
+          const swatch = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(i === 0 ? '#mirror-swatch' : '#glass-swatch')!;
+          if (!colored) { swatch.style.background = ''; return; }
+          const rgb = color.map(c => Math.round(c * 255)).join(',');
+          swatch.style.background = `radial-gradient(circle at 32% 25%, #fff, rgb(${rgb}) 43%, #263626 100%)`;
+        });
+      }
+      if (data.type === 'progress') progress.style.width = `${data.progress * 100}%`;
+      if (data.type === 'frame') {
+        if (!hasFrame) { canvas.width = width; canvas.height = height; }
+        hasFrame = true;
+        context.putImageData(new ImageData(new Uint8ClampedArray(data.pixels), width, height), 0, 0);
+        sampleStatus.textContent = `${data.samples} / ${total} samples`;
+        if (data.done) {
+          clearInterval(timer);
+          elapsed.textContent = `${((performance.now() - started) / 1000).toFixed(1)}s`;
+          state.textContent = 'Render complete';
+          dot.style.background = '#709665';
+          worker?.terminate();
+        }
+      }
+      if (data.type === 'error') fail(data.message);
+    };
+    worker.postMessage({ width, height, samples: total, seed, colored });
+  } catch (error) { fail(String(error)); }
+}
+
+document.querySelector('#randomize')!.addEventListener('click', () => {
+  colored = true;
+  seed = crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint32Array(1))[0];
+  render();
+});
+document.querySelector('#reset')!.addEventListener('click', () => {
+  colored = false; seed = 420; samples.value = '64'; resolution.value = '640'; render();
+});
+samples.addEventListener('change', render);
+resolution.addEventListener('change', render);
+document.querySelector('#download')!.addEventListener('click', async () => {
+  const link = document.createElement('a');
+  link.download = `smallpt-${colored ? seed : 'original'}.png`;
+  if (hasFrame) link.href = canvas.toDataURL('image/png');
+  else {
+    const response = await fetch(`${base}render-preview.png`);
+    link.href = URL.createObjectURL(await response.blob());
+  }
+  link.click();
+  if (link.href.startsWith('blob:')) setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(link.href), 1000);
+});
+document.querySelector('#expand-button')!.addEventListener('click', async () => {
+  const area = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>('#canvas-area')!;
+  try { if (document.fullscreenElement) await document.exitFullscreen(); else await area.requestFullscreen(); }
+  catch { state.textContent = 'Fullscreen unavailable'; }
+});
+const dialog = document.querySelector<HTMLDialogElement>('#about-dialog')!;
+document.querySelector('#about-button')!.addEventListener('click', () => dialog.showModal());
+document.querySelector('#close-about')!.addEventListener('click', () => dialog.close());
+dialog.addEventListener('click', event => { if (event.target === dialog) { const rect = dialog.getBoundingClientRect(); if (event.clientX < rect.left || event.clientX > rect.right || event.clientY < rect.top || event.clientY > rect.bottom) dialog.close(); } });
+window.addEventListener('pagehide', () => { worker?.terminate(); clearInterval(timer); });
+render();

+# Rewards registration integration
+
+This project is served as static files and has no membership backend. The form supports three steps and local validation. It deliberately reports that registration is unavailable rather than claiming to create an account or sending credentials to a static host. Fields are disabled if JavaScript is unavailable. User details are kept only in the page, never in cookies, browser storage, analytics, or console logs.
+
+To connect production enrollment:
+
+1. Serve the page over HTTPS. Set the form's `data-endpoint` to a same-origin registration endpoint, and inject a session-bound token into `<meta name="csrf-token" content="SERVER_GENERATED_TOKEN">`. Do not hardcode a token in this repository or deploy this page with a shared cached token.
+2. Accept POST multipart form data with `name`, `email`, `password`, optional `favorite` and `marketing`, `terms=accepted`, and the empty `website` honeypot. Verify the `X-CSRF-Token` against the session and validate Origin server-side before processing. Use Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite session cookies.
+3. Independently validate all fields, password length (15–128 characters), explicit consent, allowed coffee preferences, and the honeypot. Apply rate limits and abuse controls. Enforce unique accounts, handle retries safely, and return generic responses that do not reveal membership status. Hash passwords using a suitable password-hashing algorithm such as Argon2id; never log passwords or request bodies.
+4. Send an expiring, single-use email verification link. Return JSON `{"status":"verification_required"}` on acceptance. The frontend treats all other success payloads and HTTP errors as unconfirmed registration, preserves the entered values, and offers a retry. A timeout may follow a successful server write, so the backend must handle retries safely.
+5. Set `Cache-Control: no-store` for account responses. Configure a Content Security Policy, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, and other security headers at the hosting layer. Supply the actual rewards terms and privacy policy at the linked routes before launch.
+
+Client validation is a usability feature, not a security boundary. There is no production enrollment implementation in this static repository.

+
+The static site implements the complete registration UI. It does not create accounts without a backend. Failed or unavailable requests display an error and retain entered values in memory for retry. No registration data is saved in local storage, URLs, or logs.

+- `GET /api/csrf`: return `application/json` with `{ "csrfToken": "session-bound token" }`. Use `Cache-Control: no-store` and a Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite session cookie.
+- `POST /api/rewards`: accept JSON containing `givenName`, `familyName`, `email`, `password`, `favorite`, `marketing`, and `terms`. Validate the session-bound `X-CSRF-Token` header and request origin. Return a successful HTTP status and `{ "success": true }` only when the account is accepted and an email activation message is queued. Return 429 for rate limiting and appropriate error statuses otherwise. Do not redirect these API requests.

+The backend must independently validate and limit every field: nonblank names up to 80 characters each, valid email up to 254 characters, password of 12–128 characters, accepted terms, a boolean marketing choice, and an allowed favorite drink. Hash passwords using a suitable password hashing algorithm such as Argon2id; never log passwords or raw request bodies. Apply request size limits, abuse protection, verification email controls, and generic account responses to avoid disclosing existing members. Confirm email ownership before activating rewards.
+
+Deploy with a suitable Content-Security-Policy (allow this site's scripts and styles and images.unsplash.com images), HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and frame-ancestors restrictions. Existing policy, account, menu, and location links require real routes in the hosting application.

+# Script performance diagnostics
+
+The page loads `script-performance.js` without blocking HTML parsing. It observes
+long animation frames (frames over 50 ms) and aggregates their script attribution
+by source URL for the current page visit, including buffered entries from before
+the monitor registered. No data is transmitted or persisted.
+
+In the developer console, run:
+
+```js
+scriptPerformance.report(); // Ranked scripts with at least 100 ms accumulated
+scriptPerformance.report({ minDurationMs: 0 }); // All observed scripts
+scriptPerformance.snapshot(); // Same data without console output
+```
+
+A report is also logged when the tab becomes hidden. Reports show invocation
+count, accumulated duration, longest invocation, and forced style/layout time
+(a portion of duration, not an extra cost). Start with the highest accumulated
+duration and use the source URL to investigate the script. Data accumulates
+across observer callbacks; reading a report does not reset it.
+
+The monitor retains at most 200 source URLs to bound memory. Reports include an
+`overflowInvocations` count when additional sources are omitted. Returned rows
+are copies, so modifying a snapshot does not affect later reports.
+
+This measures script work attributed to slow frames, not network download time,
+all JavaScript execution, or definitive causation. Frames can also be slow due to
+rendering. Some work has no attribution (including workers and cross-origin
+iframes), and an empty source URL is grouped as unattributed. Source URLs identify
+entry points, not necessarily the slowest nested function. See the
+[Long Animation Frames API documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Performance_API/Long_animation_frame_timing).
+
+Unsupported browsers keep the page working; `snapshot().supported` is `false`
+and `report()` explains that attribution is unavailable. An empty supported
+report means no attributed scripts met the threshold, not proof the page is fast.
+The original page contains no scripts to diagnose; no artificial slow code is added.
+
+Run the isolated monitor checks with `node --test script-performance.test.cjs`.

+# The Daily Grind: field INP monitoring
+
+The homepage loads `assets/inp-monitor.js`, a self-hosted, deferred module built
+from `src/inp-monitor.mjs` and Google's `web-vitals/attribution`. Its observers
+measure real interactions throughout the visit, including bfcache restores.
+There are no synthetic interactions, polling timers, or visible page changes.
+
+## Connect production collection
+
+This repository is a static site and has no telemetry backend. Deploy a collector
+or a same-origin proxy to your analytics service, then set its URL in `index.html`:
+
+```html
+<meta name="inp-endpoint" content="/analytics/inp">
+```
+
+The collector must accept POST bodies containing JSON sent as `text/plain`
+(the browser's default for a string body) and return a successful status. Only
+same-origin endpoints are accepted. Until configured, no network reports are
+sent. Every report also emits `window`'s `daily-grind:inp` CustomEvent, with the
+serializable report in `event.detail`, for an existing analytics integration.
+
+Native `fetchLater()` replaces pending snapshots and defers delivery until the
+visitor leaves. A fallback sends on document visibility becoming hidden using
+`sendBeacon`, with keepalive fetch if the beacon queue rejects the request.
+Quota exceptions from native deferred fetch also use this fallback. Delivery is
+best effort; there is no persistent retry queue or delivery acknowledgement.
+
+Upsert by `id`, accepting only a greater `sequence` for that ID. Reports are
+snapshots: use `value`, not a sum or maximum of updates. A new ID represents a new
+metric instance, including after bfcache restoration. `reportAllChanges` reports
+INP candidate changes, **not every interaction**. A visit without qualifying
+interactions (or without Event Timing support) produces no INP measurement.
+
+## Diagnose slow interactions
+
+All durations are milliseconds. Group the latest snapshots by `page`, target,
+and script URL/function; compute field p75 across visits. Good INP is at most
+200 ms, needs improvement is above 200 through 500 ms, and poor is above 500 ms.
+Keep good visits in the dataset to avoid biasing the distribution.
+
+- `phases` separates input delay, event processing, and presentation delay.
+- `interaction` records a static `data-inp-target` label (or element tag), type,
+  relative timestamp, and load state. Labels cover every homepage link.
+- `attribution.longestScript` identifies the largest overlapping script, its
+  source URL, function, character position, invoker type, INP subpart, overlapping
+  duration, and forced style/layout costs. This is diagnostic overlap, not proof
+  of causality; source positions refer to deployed scripts.
+- `totalScriptDuration`, `totalStyleAndLayoutDuration`, `totalPaintDuration`,
+  and `totalUnattributedDuration` are the library's interaction timing buckets.
+- `renderStyleDuration` and `renderLayoutDuration` sum rendering costs across
+  **whole intersecting long frames**. They may extend outside the interaction;
+  do not add them to the INP phases or to the combined style/layout total.
+- Separate style/layout timings are experimental. Missing values are `null`;
+  use combined `forcedStyleAndLayoutDuration` and `totalStyleAndLayoutDuration`
+  on browsers without the split fields. Without Long Animation Frame support,
+  INP and its phases still report but script/render attribution is unavailable.
+  `loafSupported` distinguishes unsupported browsers from zero captured frames.
+
+No text content, input values, DOM IDs, page queries, or fragments are collected.
+Script URLs exclude credentials, query parameters, and fragments. Review script
+paths and function names under your analytics data policy before collection.
+
+## Build and automated checks
+
+```sh
+pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+pnpm test
+pnpm run build
+```
+
+The generated bundle is committed so the existing static hosting command works
+without a runtime dependency install. Rebuild and commit `assets/inp-monitor.js`
+when its source or dependencies change. Serve that file with revalidation
+(`Cache-Control: no-cache`) so updates are picked up. No server is needed for
+these checks. Tests cover timing serialization, unavailable timings, snapshot
+replacement, page lifecycle delivery, and transport fallbacks.
+
+Reference: [Google's web-vitals attribution documentation](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/web-vitals#attribution-build).

@@ -0,0 +1,54 @@
+# Daily Grind performance audit
+
+Audited 2026-11-06. Scope: the supplied static homepage, its assets and package configuration. Validation uses source inspection, downloaded asset sizes, file metadata and a dependency-free resource check. No browser, dev/preview server, server entrypoint or Lighthouse run was used. This project has no build script; no build was required.
+
+## Findings and changes
+
+| Area | Finding | Resolution |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| LCP discovery | The hero was a CSS background, without a preload or priority hint. Its request depended on CSS processing. | Put the image in the initial HTML as a `picture` with one eager, high-priority `img`. The preload scanner can discover it directly. No redundant image preload is needed. |
+| Image delivery | Every viewport referenced the same 1350 × 900 remote image. The sampled response was a 157,968-byte JPEG. | Self-host the same photograph in AVIF with a WebP fallback, with 640, 960, 1280 and 1920px candidates. `sizes` accounts for full-width desktop display, portrait `object-fit: cover` cropping and the minimum hero height. |
+| Network chain | The hero required a connection to `images.unsplash.com`. | All render resources are now same-origin or inline. There are no third-party runtime requests. |
+| Layout stability | The original hero already reserved space, but mobile browser toolbar changes could resize its `vh` height. | Preserve reserved hero geometry, include intrinsic image dimensions, use stable `svh` with a `vh` fallback and retain a dark background while loading. Keep the photo outside content flow. |
+| Mobile interactions | The single-row navigation could overflow; links had small touch targets. | Wrap navigation links below 800px, provide 44px-tall navigation targets and let the product grid shrink below its previous 250px floor. Scale the hero heading for narrow screens. |
+| INP / main thread | No client JavaScript, event handlers, timers, hydration, DOM measurement loops or third-party widgets exist in this repository. | Preserve native link interactions and zero JavaScript. No evidence of a script-based slow interaction exists to fix; destination latency requires deployment data. |
+| CSS / fonts | The page uses a small inline stylesheet and system fonts, with no CSS imports or external styles. | Preserve this short rendering path. Do not add a framework, font downloads, content-visibility or a service worker for this small page. |
+| Asset versioning | Previously the image was remotely managed. | Commit image files with content hashes, enabling safe immutable asset caching when configured on the host. |
+
+## Measured payloads
+
+These are file sizes, **not measured Core Web Vitals or load times**. Browser image selection depends on viewport, pixel density, cover cropping and format support. Only one picture candidate is normally downloaded, not the whole table.
+
+| Width | AVIF bytes | WebP bytes |
+| --- | ---: | ---: |
+| 640 | 17,513 | 30,450 |
+| 960 | 27,407 | 52,788 |
+| 1280 | 39,023 | 83,756 |
+| 1920 | 65,383 | 177,082 |
+
+Compared with the sampled original JPEG, the 1280px AVIF is 75.3% smaller and the 640px AVIF is 88.9% smaller. These comparisons use different resolutions and compression settings; they do not establish equal visual quality. The largest AVIF is still 58.6% smaller than the original. The 1920px WebP is larger than the original because it supplies a higher resolution; smaller WebP candidates reduce transfer for smaller displays.
+
+The final inline HTML/CSS is approximately 6.4 KB uncompressed (original: 4,708 bytes). Client JavaScript remains 0 bytes. The slightly larger markup exposes responsive image candidates and adds mobile layout rules. No extra blocking stylesheet request was introduced.
+
+## Validation
+
+Run `npm run check:performance`. It reads files only and verifies:
+
+- Hero priority, eager loading, decorative semantics and intrinsic dimensions.
+- Matching AVIF/WebP sizing policies and all eight local candidates.
+- Image signatures, encoded widths, the fallback image height and SHA-256 filename fingerprints.
+- Per-file budgets of 75 KB for AVIF, 190 KB for WebP and 12 KB for HTML/CSS.
+- No missing or unreferenced image files, runtime scripts, remote CSS backgrounds or external blocking stylesheets.
+
+Also run `git diff --check`. Source comparison confirms the existing text and all navigation destinations are retained. These checks protect resource delivery; they cannot verify paint timing, visual quality, viewport behavior, real input latency or browser CLS.
+
+## Deployment considerations and remaining measurements
+
+- **Caching:** No production server configuration is supplied. Configure `/assets/coffee-hero-*` with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and the public homepage with `Cache-Control: no-cache` so it revalidates. Do not apply public caching to account/logout responses. These headers have not been configured or verified by this change.
+- **Compression and transport:** Enable Brotli or gzip for HTML at the host and verify MIME types (`image/avif`, `image/webp`). Image files are already compressed. TTFB, redirects, HTTP version, CDN behavior and actual response headers cannot be inferred from local source.
+- **Core Web Vitals:** No LCP, INP, CLS or Lighthouse score is claimed. After deployment, use available field data to assess mobile/desktop LCP, INP and CLS at the 75th percentile, and separate LCP into TTFB, resource delay, download time and render delay. Use existing analytics or CrUX/Search Console if available; no tracking script was added.
+- **Destinations:** `/menu`, `/locations`, `/rewards`, `/account`, `/logout`, `/order-online` and other linked pages have no implementations in the supplied repository. Their response times and interaction behavior are outside the evidence available here. Links are preserved. Avoid automatic prefetch/prerender of account, ordering or logout URLs, which can trigger unintended work or side effects.
+
+## Photograph provenance
+
+The assets use the same existing Unsplash photograph: `https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1495474472287-4d71bcdd2085`. Variants were downloaded with `fm=avif&q=50` or `fm=webp&q=55`, `fit=crop` and the indicated width. The original aspect ratio and centered cover treatment are preserved. No generated imagery was used.

@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+# Daily Grind performance audit
+
+## Scope and findings
+
+Audited the complete checkout: one static HTML page, inline CSS, system fonts, and one external hero background. No application JavaScript, hydration, third-party scripts, font downloads, interaction handlers, or build pipeline exist. No browser, server, or server entrypoint was used. This is a source and asset audit; LCP, INP, CLS, TTFB, and Lighthouse scores have **not** been measured.
+
+The main loading opportunity was the CSS hero background: a single 1350-pixel image on Unsplash, with no responsive selection or explicit priority. The original URL returned 157,968 bytes during this audit; its `auto=format` response can vary by client. Remote image delivery also required a separate origin connection. The page's inline styles and system fonts already avoid additional blocking stylesheet and font requests.
+
+The desktop navigation could exceed a narrow viewport. Its sticky positioning also consumed mobile screen space. No slow JavaScript interaction can be established from this source. All 13 navigation destinations are absent from the checkout; backend routing and destination response times remain unverified. A missing destination or slow navigation response is distinct from INP, which measures interaction responsiveness on the current page.
+
+## Changes
+
+- Reused the existing stock photograph as local WebP variants. No third-party requests remain in page resources.
+- Replaced the CSS background with an early, parser-discoverable `img`, using `srcset`, `sizes`, `fetchpriority="high"`, and eager loading. No redundant preload is needed for this image in the initial markup. Decorative empty alt text preserves the background's semantics.
+- Preserved the centered cover image, dark overlay, colors, content, and native links. Explicit image dimensions and a hero height independent of image download reserve space. A minimum hero height keeps text and the CTA inside the hero on short screens.
+- Wrapped navigation with stable CSS breakpoints and retained sticky navigation on desktop. Increased link target space, added visible keyboard focus, and respected reduced motion. No JavaScript was introduced.
+- Made the card grid fit viewports narrower than its previous 250-pixel minimum track size.
+- Added a dependency-free offline resource inventory and byte budgets: `npm run audit:performance`. It checks resource availability, WebP signatures, third-party dependencies, HTML size, and individual resource sizes. Missing application routes are reported separately because deployment routing is unknown.
+
+## Asset measurements
+
+| Hero candidate | Bytes | Compared with original response |
+| --- | ---: | ---: |
+| Original remote URL | 157,968 | baseline |
+| 480 × 320 WebP | 25,812 | 83.7% smaller |
+| 960 × 640 WebP | 72,892 | 53.9% smaller |
+| 1440 × 960 WebP | 139,080 | 12.0% smaller |
+| 1920 × 1280 WebP | 177,082 | 12.1% larger, higher resolution |
+
+The browser selects one candidate according to viewport, pixel density, and its own heuristics; mobile devices do not necessarily select the smallest file. The 1920 candidate intentionally trades bytes for detail on larger or denser displays. These are uncompressed file sizes, not measured transfer timings or CWV gains. HTML gzip/Brotli sizes printed by the script are estimates; they do not prove deployment compression is enabled.
+
+## Deployment follow-up
+
+1. Configure compression for HTML on the actual host and verify cache headers. Keep HTML revalidatable. Images can use a long cache lifetime only with a versioning policy; current descriptive filenames must be renamed when their contents change before enabling immutable caching. WebP does not benefit materially from additional gzip.
+2. Verify the 13 destination routes on the deployed application, especially ordering, account, and logout. This checkout contains no route implementation or authentication backend to optimize.
+3. Use deployed field data (Search Console/CrUX or consent-appropriate real-user monitoring) to assess the 75th percentile by device: LCP ≤2.5 seconds, INP ≤200 ms, CLS ≤0.1. No monitoring script or endpoint was added without an existing telemetry integration. Hosting latency, caching, and destination performance cannot be inferred from source.
+4. If field data still shows image-related LCP delays, compare candidate selection and image quality before adding further formats or preloads. Investigate server response time if TTFB dominates. Preserve this page's zero-JavaScript baseline.
+
+Guidance: [Optimize LCP](https://web.dev/articles/optimize-lcp), [Responsive images](https://web.dev/learn/design/responsive-images), [Core Web Vitals report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9205520).
+
+## Image provenance
+
+Existing stock image: https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1495474472287-4d71bcdd2085
+
+Variants downloaded with `fm=webp&fit=crop&w=WIDTH&h=HEIGHT&q=70`, except the 1920-pixel variant uses `q=55`. Dimensions and byte sizes were verified offline. The image is served locally at runtime.

+# The Daily Grind
+
+The homepage is static HTML with a bundled client script. Seasonal Favorites are
+HTML strings in `src/homepage.mjs`. All application HTML insertion goes through
+`src/safe-html.mjs`, which uses DOMPurify with a narrow tag and attribute allowlist.
+Keep new HTML sinks behind this sanitizer and never change markup after sanitizing.
+
+The page's Content Security Policy requires Trusted Types for DOM injection sinks
+in supporting browsers and permits only DOMPurify's policy. Other browsers still
+receive sanitized markup. There is no permissive default Trusted Types policy.
+
+After changing the source or updating DOMPurify, regenerate the committed bundle:
+
+```sh
+pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+pnpm build
+pnpm test
+```
+
+Commit `assets/homepage.js` alongside source changes so the existing static hosting
+workflow works without a build step. Keep DOMPurify updated for security fixes.
+Tests use jsdom, including a Trusted Types API stub; they do not verify native
+browser CSP enforcement or launch a browser or server.

+import { createSafeHTMLRenderer } from './safe-html.mjs';
+
+const seasonalFavorites = [
+  `<div class="card">
+    <h3>Maple Oat Latte</h3>
+    <p>Creamy oat milk with a hint of Vermont maple syrup.</p>
+    <a href="/menu/seasonal" class="btn">View Details</a>
+  </div>`,
+  `<div class="card">
+    <h3>Dark Roast Espresso</h3>
+    <p>Bold, smokey, and perfect for a morning boost.</p>
+    <a href="/menu/espresso" class="btn">View Details</a>
+  </div>`,
+  `<div class="card">
+    <h3>Cold Brew</h3>
+    <p>Steeped for 18 hours for maximum smoothness.</p>
+    <a href="/menu/cold-brew" class="btn">View Details</a>

+];

+const renderHTML = createSafeHTMLRenderer(window);
+const favorites = document.getElementById('seasonal-favorites');
+
+if (favorites) {
+  renderHTML(favorites, seasonalFavorites.join(''));

+import createDOMPurify from 'dompurify';
+
+// Create once per page so DOMPurify can reuse its private Trusted Types policy.
+export function createSafeHTMLRenderer(window) {
+  const purifier = createDOMPurify(window);
+
+  return (target, html) => {
+    // Keep this as the only application HTML sink. Never modify sanitized markup.
+    // TrustedHTML is returned where supported; other browsers still sanitize.
+    target.innerHTML = purifier.sanitize(html, {
+      ALLOWED_TAGS: ['div', 'h3', 'p', 'a'],
+      ALLOWED_ATTR: ['class', 'href'],
+      ALLOW_DATA_ATTR: false,
+      ALLOW_ARIA_ATTR: false,
+      RETURN_TRUSTED_TYPE: true,
+    });
+  };
+}

+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
+import test from 'node:test';
+import { JSDOM } from 'jsdom';
+import { createSafeHTMLRenderer } from '../src/safe-html.mjs';
+
+const page = await readFile(new URL('../index.html', import.meta.url), 'utf8');
+
+test('the shipped bundle renders the original three favorites and destinations', async () => {
+  const dom = new JSDOM(page, { runScripts: 'outside-only' });
+  try {
+    const bundle = await readFile(new URL('../assets/homepage.js', import.meta.url), 'utf8');
+    dom.window.eval(bundle);
+    const cards = [...dom.window.document.querySelectorAll('#seasonal-favorites .card')];
+    assert.deepEqual(cards.map(card => card.querySelector('h3').textContent), [
+      'Maple Oat Latte', 'Dark Roast Espresso', 'Cold Brew',
+    ]);
+    assert.deepEqual(cards.map(card => card.querySelector('a').getAttribute('href')), [
+      '/menu/seasonal', '/menu/espresso', '/menu/cold-brew',
+    ]);
+    assert.ok(cards.every(card => card.querySelector('p').textContent.length > 0));
+  } finally {
+    dom.window.close();
+  }
+});
+
+test('the HTML sink removes executable markup and preserves permitted card content', () => {
+  const dom = new JSDOM('<div id="target"></div>');
+  try {
+    const target = dom.window.document.getElementById('target');
+    const render = createSafeHTMLRenderer(dom.window);
+    render(target, `<div class="card" onclick="alert(1)" id="location" style="color:red">
+      <h3>Safe coffee</h3><p>Still here</p>
+      <script>alert(1)</script><img src=x onerror="alert(1)">
+      <svg><g onload="alert(1)"></g></svg>
+      <math><mtext><img src=x onerror="alert(1)"></mtext></math>
+      <iframe srcdoc="<script>alert(1)</script>"></iframe>
+      <form><input name="innerHTML"></form>
+      <a class="btn" href="/menu/seasonal">View Details</a>
+    </div>`);
+    assert.equal(target.querySelector('h3').textContent, 'Safe coffee');
+    assert.equal(target.querySelector('p').textContent, 'Still here');
+    assert.equal(target.querySelector('a').getAttribute('href'), '/menu/seasonal');
+    for (const element of target.querySelectorAll('*')) {
+      assert.ok(['DIV', 'H3', 'P', 'A'].includes(element.tagName));
+      assert.ok([...element.attributes].every(attr => ['class', 'href'].includes(attr.name)));
+    }
+    render(target, '<p>Replacement</p>');
+    assert.equal(target.innerHTML, '<p>Replacement</p>');
+  } finally {
+    dom.window.close();
+  }
+});
+
+test('the HTML sink strips obfuscated script URLs', () => {
+  const dom = new JSDOM('<div></div>');
+  try {
+    const target = dom.window.document.querySelector('div');
+    const render = createSafeHTMLRenderer(dom.window);
+    for (const href of ['javascript:alert(1)', 'javascript:alert(1)', 'java
script:alert(1)', 'vbscript:msgbox(1)', 'data:text/html,<script>alert(1)</script>']) {
+      render(target, `<a href="${href}">Details</a>`);
+      assert.equal(target.querySelector('a').getAttribute('href'), null, href);
+    }
+  } finally {
+    dom.window.close();
+  }
+});
+
+test('Trusted Types integration passes sanitized TrustedHTML to the sink', () => {
+  const dom = new JSDOM('<div></div>');
+  try {
+    const policies = [];
+    class TrustedHTML {
+      constructor(value) { this.value = value; }
+      toString() { return this.value; }
+    }
+    dom.window.trustedTypes = {
+      createPolicy(name, rules) {
+        policies.push(name);
+        return {
+          createHTML: value => new TrustedHTML(rules.createHTML(value)),
+          createScriptURL: value => rules.createScriptURL(value),
+        };
+      },
+    };
+    const render = createSafeHTMLRenderer(dom.window);
+    let inserted;
+    const target = { set innerHTML(value) { inserted = value; } };
+    render(target, '<p onclick="alert(1)">Coffee</p><script>alert(1)</script>');
+    assert.ok(inserted instanceof TrustedHTML);
+    assert.equal(String(inserted), '<p>Coffee</p>');
+    render(target, '<p>Again</p>');
+    assert.deepEqual(policies, ['dompurify']);
+  } finally {
+    dom.window.close();
+  }
+});
+
+test('CSP enforces Trusted Types and permits only the sanitizer policy', () => {
+  const dom = new JSDOM(page);
+  try {
+    const policy = dom.window.document.querySelector('meta[http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy"]').content;
+    const directives = policy.split(';').map(value => value.trim());
+    assert.ok(directives.includes("require-trusted-types-for 'script'"));
+    assert.ok(directives.includes('trusted-types dompurify'));
+    assert.ok(directives.includes("script-src 'self'"));
+    assert.ok(directives.includes("object-src 'none'"));
+    assert.ok(directives.includes("base-uri 'none'"));
+  } finally {
+    dom.window.close();
+  }
+});
